stem: Which statement about glove use and hand hygiene is correct?

options.A: Gloves replace hand hygiene whenever intact gloves are worn.
options.B: Hand hygiene is unnecessary after glove removal if no visible contamination is present.
options.C: Hand hygiene before donning gloves is unnecessary whenever gloves are indicated.
options.D: When a task requires gloves, perform hand hygiene before donning them and always clean the hands after glove removal.

rationale: CDC states that gloves are not a substitute for hand hygiene. When a task requires gloves, hand hygiene should be performed before donning them and touching the patient or surroundings, and hands should always be cleaned after glove removal. D is correct.
educational_objective: Apply CDC hand-hygiene requirements before and after glove use.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Clinical Safety: Hand Hygiene for Healthcare Workers
source_locator: Know when to wear (and change) gloves
source_claim_supported: Gloves are not a substitute for hand hygiene; perform hand hygiene before donning gloves when the task requires them and always after glove removal.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — hand hygiene and standard precautions
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — hand hygiene with gloves

source_original.stem: A new nurse states that hand hygiene is unnecessary as long as gloves are worn. The charge nurse should correct this misconception by explaining:

options.A: Gloves replace hand hygiene whenever intact gloves are worn for direct patient contact
options.B: Hand hygiene is unnecessary after glove removal when no visible contamination is present
options.C: Skip gloves whenever hand hygiene was performed immediately before a patient-care task
options.D: Perform hand hygiene before donning gloves when indicated and immediately after removal

source_original.rationale: Wearing gloves does not eliminate the need for hand hygiene. Hand hygiene should be performed before donning gloves and immediately after removing them, since gloves can have small, sometimes undetectable defects, and hands can become contaminated during the glove removal process itself.
source_original.source_detail: Gloves are not a substitute for hand hygiene; clean hands before donning gloves when indicated and immediately after glove removal; accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Removed the new-nurse cue and aligned the wording exactly with current CDC glove/hand-hygiene recommendations.

audit_findings.claim_audit: Final D directly matches CDC guidance.

distractor_audit.C: False; hand hygiene does not replace indicated gloves.

audit_findings.blueprint: Hand hygiene fits Safety and Infection Prevention and Control.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked current CDC glove section; D remains unique.
